title: Development of RT-qPCR for quantification of human enterovirus D68 in vitro

steps.title: Prepare A549 growth medium
steps.instruction: In a laminar‑flow cabinet mix DMEM/F‑12 (Gibco) with 10 % fetal bovine serum (Gibco) and 1 % Antimycotic‑Antibiotic 100X (Gibco) to the formulation recommended for ATCC CCL‑185 A549 cells; adjust pH to 7.42.

steps.title: Thaw and culture A549 cells
steps.instruction: Retrieve ATCC CCL‑185 A549 cells stored at –80 °C, thaw quickly in a 37 °C water bath, add to the prepared growth medium, and seed into a flask; incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, humidified atmosphere.

steps.title: Maintain and split A549 cultures
steps.instruction: Monitor cell confluence; when >80 % confluent, detach cells with appropriate method and reseed to keep cultures healthy for virus propagation.

steps.title: Thaw EV‑D68 virus stock
steps.instruction: Work in a biosafety cabinet, retrieve EV‑D68 (HRV87, ATCC VR‑1197™) stored at –80 °C, thaw in a 37 °C water bath, and decontaminate the ampule according to biosafety guidelines.

steps.title: Inoculate A549 cells with EV‑D68
steps.instruction: Prepare a confluent (>70 %) A549 flask, remove growth medium, wash monolayer with PBS, add 1 ml virus to 19 ml growth medium in a 50 ml tube, mix, then transfer 1 ml of this suspension to the flask containing 9 ml fresh growth medium; place the flask in a 33 °C incubator.

steps.title: Incubate infected cells and monitor CPE
steps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated flask at 33 °C; observe cytopathic effect (round, refractile cells in small clades) at 4 days post‑infection.

steps.title: Perform TCID₅₀ titration
steps.instruction: Determine the 50 % tissue‑culture infectious dose of EV‑D68 using a ten‑fold dilution series (10⁰–10⁻⁸) and a 96‑well plate assay.

substeps.instruction: Seed 5 000 A549 cells in 200 µl growth medium per well in rows 2–11 of a 96‑well plate (VWR); add 200 µl growth medium without cells to row 12 as background; rock plate gently and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

Prepare serial 1:10 dilutions of the virus stock in tubes containing 3.6 ml growth medium; transfer 400 µl of virus to the first tube, then 400 µl from each tube to the next to obtain dilutions from 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁷ (or as needed).

Label the plate lid with a grid to indicate quadruplicate wells for each dilution; remove medium from each well, add 200 µl of the appropriate virus dilution to each well (working backwards through the dilution series).
Incubate the plate at 33 °C for 5 days, monitoring for CPE.

When the endpoint is reached (CPE consistent across three readings per dilution), discard medium, wash cells with 100 µl DPBS (Sigma), fix with 50 µl methanol for 1 min, discard methanol, then add 100 µl 0.1 % crystal violet in distilled water for 20 min.
Wash plates and measure absorbance at 570 nm with a plate reader.
Calculate TCID₅₀ using the Reed‑Muench method.

steps.title: Extract viral RNA (RNeasy protocol)
steps.instruction: Isolate RNA from infected cell culture using a modified Qiagen RNeasy Plus Mini Kit (no G‑column).

substeps.instruction: Add 350 µl RLT buffer to a 2 ml Eppendorf tube (G‑column step omitted).
Add 100 µl of the virus‑containing sample to the RLT buffer.
Add 450 µl (1 volume) 70 % ethanol, vortex gently.

Transfer up to 700 µl of the lysate to an RNeasy Mini spin column in a 2 ml collection tube; centrifuge 15 s at ≥8000 × g, discard flow‑through. Repeat with remaining lysate using a new collection tube.
Add 700 µl RWI buffer, centrifuge 15 s at ≥8000 × g, discard flow‑through.
Add 500 µl RPE buffer, centrifuge 15 s at ≥8000 × g, discard flow‑through.
Add another 500 µl RPE buffer, centrifuge 2 min at ≥8000 × g, discard flow‑through.
Place the spin column in a clean 1.5 ml tube, add 40 µl RNase‑free water, centrifuge 1 min at ≥8000 × g to elute RNA.
Discard the spin column, close the tube, store RNA at –80 °C; optionally quantify RNA with a Qubit 4.0 fluorometer.

steps.title: Prepare primers and probe
steps.instruction: Dilute forward (FWD) and reverse (RWD) primers to a working stock of 100 nM; for assay optimization test primer concentrations from 200 nM to 600 nM and probe concentrations from 200 nM (initial) to 100–600 nM; use the MGB‑FAM probe (sequence TCC AAA TCT CGC ATT GAA CCG GT) from Applied Biosystems.

steps.title: Set up one‑step RT‑qPCR reactions
steps.instruction: Assemble 15 µl reactions using Quantabio qScript XLT One‑Step RT‑qPCR ToughMix (low ROX) with the following per‑well volumes: 7.5 µl 1X master mix, 1.8 µl probe (300 nM final), 1.2 µl reverse primer (400 nM final), 0.92 µl forward primer (300 nM final), 1.0 µl RNA sample (1X), and 2.6 µl RNase‑free water; include a positive viral control, a no‑template control (NTC), and a ROX reference dye.

steps.title: Prepare standard curve dilutions
steps.instruction: Make a series of 10‑fold dilutions of an in‑vitro‑transcribed EV‑D68 RNA reference in RNase‑free water to generate a standard curve and determine the limit of detection.

steps.title: Load plate, centrifuge, and run qPCR
steps.instruction: Dispense reactions into a 96‑well MicroAmp plate (Applied Biosystems), seal with Optical Adhesive Film, centrifuge 40 s at 34 × 100 rpm, then place the plate in an Agilent AriaMx Real‑Time PCR instrument.

substeps.instruction: Run the following thermal profile: reverse transcription 10 min at 50 °C; initial denaturation 1 min at 95 °C; 40 cycles of 95 °C for 10 s followed by 60 °C for 1 min.
Collect fluorescence data for each well.

steps.title: Analyze qPCR data
steps.instruction: Calculate Cq values, generate standard curves, and determine efficiency (slope between –3.0 and –3.8, R² > 0.99); identify the limit of detection (Cq ≈ 18.405 corresponds to TCID₅₀ = 10⁵); confirm specificity by lack of signal in uninfected controls.

description: The MIQE guidelines [13] refer to a common standard that is used in work to establish new PCR methods. For the preparation of RT-qPCR, the method must be validated based on sensitivity, specificity, precision, and efficiency. The validation parameters are evaluated based on the choice of reagents, optimization of primer and probe, and establishment of a standard curve. In this study, we first validated the assay in a one-step RT-qPCR format using serial dilutions of an In Vitro transcribed RNA reference. One-step RT-qPCR was decided to use throughout the study because the advantages of limited contamination and simplicity account for better conditions than the disadvantages compared to two-step RT-qPCR. For one-step reactions, all reagents are added in the same well on the PCR plate. Conversion from RNA to the more stable cDNA takes place internally in a closed environment and as a result, excludes consideration of the reverse transcriptase step and controls that convert RNA into cDNA.
